meta.move: Secret: evidence lands on the late night
meta.expect: After the times, she goes shorter and harder, to procedure (who decided, 4.2); does not ask about that night again; no laptop; debrief says how close it came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong, and I own it.

Here's the version history. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58 PM another 794. Then small edits. No earlier drafts.

11:31, 11:52 with 612 words, 11:58 with 794: I'm writing that down. Students draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale, so that shows where the words landed, not who wrote them. And under 4.1, did you speak to Owen before that zero went in?
So he wrote nothing until almost midnight the night before it was due, and then fourteen hundred words appeared in six minutes.
That's your conclusion, not your document, Hale; it shows nothing about what he wrote before that file existed. You haven't answered me about whether Owen was heard first.
What was he doing at midnight that night?
I'm not the one being questioned, Hale. You've had a week since you entered that zero, so tell me who decided it and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, and a clear answer on who decided it and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position: she agreed to nothing and still wants the zero withdrawn and an answer on whether Owen was heard first; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you ended before her time ran out, so there was still room to get there.
What moved her: Owning in one sentence that the zero went in before you called, then showing the version history with exact times and word counts; that got a flat okay and had her writing it down, because it was specific, dated and tied to Owen's own file.
What cost ground: Asking what Owen was doing at midnight; that turned her into a witness about her own home, which she will never be, and it let her pivot to your unanswered procedure question.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on the night of October 28 between 11:31 and 11:58 PM, very close to that kind of late night, which is why she went shorter and harder; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students draft elsewhere and paste it in, answer that defence with something she can check, such as comparing the essay with Owen's other work under 4.3, tell her plainly whether you spoke to Owen first under 4.1, and then offer the 4.4 rewrite in writing.
